threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and initial task ownership for the playbook project.

messages.text: Kicking off the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout project_title. Goal is to have a unified way of working across sales and the contact centre within 30 days, with a one-month pilot in between. For the pilot KPIs, my initial proposal is: 1) conversion rate on qualified opportunities, 2) first contact resolution for top 5 contact reasons, 3) average handle time with a guardrail so we do not push it down at the expense of quality, 4) contact-to-opportunity handover speed between contact centre and sales, and 5) agent adherence to scripts and CRM data completeness. We can track most of this in the Pilot KPIs and Performance Tracking Sheet A4. For scope, I suggest we start with T1 to T4 as the core: journey mapping, qualification checklist, call scripts, and email/chat templates. Can you all react to the KPI list and confirm you are ok owning your respective tasks T1 to T4 so we can lock D1 and D2 later today

Thanks for framing this. On the contact centre side, I can take the lead on T1 and T3, since they are closer to our day-to-day. For KPIs, I would add one more for service quality, maybe QA score based on a simple checklist during the pilot, even if the full checklist T11 comes later. For first contact resolution, we need to be clear how we define it in the journeys we map in T1, otherwise reporting in A4 will be inconsistent. I am fine with the pilot being one month, but we should confirm which teams are in scope later when we talk about T8.

I can support on T1 and T3 as well, especially around documenting the current inbound and outbound flows and checking them against consumer protection and company policy. We need to make sure the new scripts in T3 do not create any risk there. On KPIs, I agree with conversion rate and first contact resolution. I am a bit unsure how we will measure adherence to scripts in the first version, unless we already have a basic monitoring form. Maybe we can start with a lighter view and refine once A6 is ready.

On the sales side, I can own T2 and T4. For T2, I will draft the qualification and needs analysis checklist and make sure it lines up with how we already use the CRM, so it is not extra work. For KPIs, I would like to see a metric around opportunity quality, maybe percentage of opportunities that move from qualification to proposal, so we know if the checklist A2 is actually helping. For handover speed, we should define a clear target, for example, sales to pick up high-value leads within one business day, but we can refine that when we talk about T10.

I can back up on T2 and T4 as well, especially testing the templates in real cases once we have a first draft. On KPIs, I like the idea of tracking conversion from qualification to proposal and also maybe a simple customer satisfaction pulse during the pilot, even if it is just a short survey after calls or emails. That would give us a more direct view of customer experience alongside the operational metrics in A4.

Good call on QA score. How about we define pilot KPIs as: 1) conversion rate from qualified opportunity to sale, 2) first contact resolution for top 5 reasons, 3) average handle time with a soft target, 4) handover speed from contact centre to sales for high-value leads, 5) CRM data completeness on mandatory fields, and 6) QA score based on a light checklist. Opportunity quality and customer satisfaction can be tracked where possible but not treated as hard success criteria for D1. Does that feel realistic for a one-month pilot

Yes, that list works for me. For first contact resolution and QA score, I will make sure T1 captures the definitions clearly so we can apply them consistently. For CRM data completeness, we will need T5 to be aligned, but I know that comes in the next thread. For now, I am ok using the existing CRM fields and just clarifying which ones are mandatory for the pilot.

I am aligned with that KPI set as well. For handover speed, I suggest we set an initial target of sales picking up high-value leads within one business day and standard leads within two business days during the pilot. We can refine the thresholds when we define escalation criteria in T10, but at least A4 will have a clear expectation to track against.

I am ok with that KPI list as long as we keep an eye on any compliance-related issues that might show up in QA reviews. If we see patterns there, we may need to adjust scripts in T3 quickly. For the pilot success criteria, maybe we can agree on minimum thresholds, like no drop in QA score and at least a small uplift in conversion, rather than very aggressive targets in the first month.

From a sales perspective, I would be comfortable if we define pilot success as: stable or better QA and customer satisfaction, no negative impact on handle time, and a measurable uplift in conversion and handover speed compared to the baseline in A4. We can set the exact numbers once we see the baseline, but at least we know what direction we want.

Summarising what I am hearing so we can close D1. Pilot KPIs: conversion rate from qualified opportunity to sale, first contact resolution for top 5 reasons, average handle time, handover speed for high-value and standard leads, CRM data completeness on mandatory fields, and QA score based on a light checklist. Success criteria: no deterioration in QA score or handle time, and a measurable uplift in conversion and handover speed versus baseline in A4. Unless anyone objects, I will record this as our agreed pilot KPI set and success criteria.

Works for me. On task ownership for D2, I propose: I take primary on T1 and T3, with support from 8337, and we aim to have first drafts ready in five working days. That should give us time to validate journeys with at least one sales account manager and start drafting scripts based on the top 5 contact reasons.

I am ok supporting you on T1 and T3. I can focus on documenting the current flows and highlighting any pain points or compliance concerns, then you can refine the scripts. Five working days for first drafts sounds achievable from my side.

On the sales tasks, I will own T2 and T4 with support from 356759. For T2, I can have a first draft of the qualification checklist ready in four working days, then share it here for review. For T4, I suggest we start with a smaller set of email and chat templates aligned with the early stages of the playbook and expand later. We can test them in at least 10 real cases as required and log results in a simple tab in A4 for now.

Confirmed, I will support on T2 and T4. I can take the lead on testing the templates in live opportunities and capturing feedback from the team. Four to five working days for first drafts is fine; that still leaves us enough time before the pilot to iterate once.

Great, then for D2 I will record: T1 and T3 owned by 269042 with support from 8337, first drafts in five working days; T2 and T4 owned by 29962 with support from 356759, first drafts in four to five working days. We will use this channel to share drafts and comments. If there are no objections, I will treat this as confirmed ownership and initial timelines.

No objections from me. I will start by pulling recent sales data to see which qualification questions correlate with better conversion, so T2 is grounded in actual outcomes. I will also check how we currently log these fields in the CRM so we do not create conflicts with T5 later.

All good on my side as well. I will start mapping the current inbound and outbound journeys for T1 today and share a first view before the end of the week so sales can validate. That will also help us prioritise which top 5 contact reasons to cover first in T3.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise scripts, qualification checklist, and CRM guidelines.

messages.text: Sharing draft materials for review so we can move towards sign-off. 1) Draft Sales Qualification and Needs Analysis Checklist A2 for T2, based on recent conversion data and current sales practices. 2) Draft unified call scripts for top 5 contact reasons from T3, compiled into the Call, Email, and Chat Script Library A5. 3) Draft CRM Data Entry and Mandatory Fields Guide A3 for T5, aligned with our current CRM configuration. Please review with a focus on practicality for agents and compliance. We need to get to a point where we can approve the checklist for the pilot D3 and sign off on the initial set of scripts D4.

I went through the call scripts in A5 and the CRM guide A3. Overall they match the journeys we mapped in T1, but I have a couple of concerns. First, some of the opening lines for complaint calls sound a bit too sales-focused; agents might struggle if the customer is already upset. Second, the mandatory fields list in A3 for inbound service calls might be too long for peak times. We risk incomplete records or longer handle times. I suggest we mark a smaller core set as truly mandatory for the pilot and keep the rest as recommended.

I agree with 269042 on the complaint scripts. From a consumer protection angle, we should start with acknowledgement and resolution before moving into any cross-sell or upsell. I also noticed one script where we ask for marketing consent quite early in the call; that might not land well and could raise questions. We should move that to the end and make sure the wording is aligned with our policy. On A3, I can help trim the list of mandatory fields for service calls so we keep what is essential for follow-up and reporting.

On the sales side, the qualification checklist A2 looks clear, but a few questions might be hard to answer on the first call, especially budget details for smaller customers. If we insist on all of them every time, we might slow down the conversation. Maybe we can mark some items as must-have for qualification and others as nice-to-have that can be filled in later, as long as we capture them before proposal stage. That would also make it easier for the contact centre when they are doing early qualification.

I tested a couple of the email templates from T4 in live cases. The structure works, but some of the follow-up emails feel a bit long. For busy customers, shorter messages with a clear call to action tend to perform better. I suggest we create a short and a long version for key stages, especially follow-up and closing, and then we can see in the pilot which ones convert better. We can track that in A4 later.

Thanks for the feedback. For the complaint scripts in A5, I will rework the openings to focus on acknowledgement and resolution first, and move any cross-sell language to the very end as optional. For A3, I like the idea of a smaller core set of mandatory fields for the pilot. We can define a core set for each interaction type and keep the rest as recommended fields that do not block call wrap-up. I will share an updated version later today.

On A2, we can split the checklist into two sections: essential qualification questions that must be answered before we create an opportunity, and additional context that can be captured before proposal. That way, contact centre agents can still qualify leads without forcing a long conversation, and sales can complete the rest later. I will mark these sections clearly in the document so it is easy to follow.

That works for us. For the CRM guide A3, can we also add a short example for each interaction type, showing a correctly filled record screenshot or description That would help agents understand what good looks like. It does not need to be perfect for the pilot, but a couple of concrete examples would reduce confusion.

I can draft the revised wording for the complaint openings and the marketing consent part and send it to you to plug into A5. I will keep it aligned with our current policy and consumer protection requirements. Once we have that, we should probably run it past compliance informally before we treat the scripts as final for the pilot, just to avoid surprises later.

I can help create the short versions of the follow-up and closing emails for T4. I will base them on the longer templates you tested and keep the key value points and call to action. During the pilot, we can alternate between short and long versions and log which ones lead to more replies or meetings, then update A5 accordingly.

Good idea. I will add one example per interaction type in A3, using anonymised data. That should make it easier for new agents during training as well. I will also make sure the mandatory fields in A3 line up with the essential questions in A2, so we are not asking for information we do not store or vice versa.

To move us towards D3 and D4, can we do a quick check. For A2, with the split between essential and additional questions, are contact centre and sales comfortable using it as the standard for the pilot For A5, assuming we adjust the complaint openings, marketing consent wording, and add short email versions, are we ok treating this as the initial approved set for the pilot, with the understanding that we can tweak based on feedback

From the contact centre side, yes. With the changes discussed, I am comfortable using A2 and A5 in the pilot. We will brief supervisors to collect feedback from agents and log any issues so we can refine scripts in the next review cycle.

I am ok as well, provided we run the updated complaint and consent wording past compliance before training. I do not expect major changes, but I would rather have their informal nod. With that condition, I support using A2 and A5 as the standard for the pilot.

On the sales side, I am comfortable with A2 and A5 as our starting point. The essential vs additional split in A2 will help a lot in practice, and having both short and long email versions will give us room to experiment during the pilot.

Given the confirmations above, I propose we formally approve A2 for use in the pilot D3 and sign off on the initial set of scripts in A5 for the pilot D4, with the understanding that we will do a quick compliance check on the updated wording and keep a feedback loop open during the pilot.

Agreed. I will note D3 and D4 as closed with the conditions we discussed. Next step is to finalise A3 for T5 so training can reference the correct mandatory fields, and to make sure A1, the unified playbook, points to A2, A3, and A5 as the standard references for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in training approach, schedule, and quality monitoring process.

messages.text: Sharing the draft Training Plan and Session Agenda A7 for T7, plus the draft Quality Monitoring Checklist for Calls A6 for T11. The training plan covers objectives, a 2-hour core session for agents and a 90-minute session for account managers, and a proposal to run sessions across shifts over one week. The QA checklist A6 is aligned with the new scripts in A5 and focuses on greeting, verification, needs analysis, solution, compliance points, and wrap-up. I need your feedback on whether the schedule is realistic with current shifts and whether the checklist is practical to use weekly.

Looking at A7, the content looks comprehensive, but I am a bit worried about the 2-hour block for agents during busy periods. We might struggle to release full teams for that long without impacting service levels. Could we split the agent training into two shorter sessions, maybe 75 minutes each, and run them on different days That might fit better with shift patterns. On A6, I like that compliance points are clearly marked, but we should make sure the scoring is simple enough so supervisors can complete reviews quickly.

For account managers, the 90-minute session in A7 is fine, but I would like to add a short segment on how to use the qualification checklist A2 and CRM guide A3 in practice, with a couple of role plays. That will help make sure we are consistent with the contact centre. Also, can we schedule the sales sessions slightly later in the rollout week so we can incorporate any early feedback from the first agent sessions

On A6, the checklist is clear, but there are quite a few items. If we want supervisors to review calls weekly for each agent, we might need a lighter version for the pilot. Maybe we can mark a subset of critical behaviours and compliance points as mandatory to score every time, and treat the rest as optional comments. That would make it easier to keep up with the review cadence.

From a scheduling point of view, splitting the agent training into two shorter sessions makes sense. We can also consider a short follow-up huddle after the first week of the pilot to capture questions and reinforce key points. For the QA checklist A6, I agree we should keep it lean for the pilot and then expand once everyone is comfortable with the basics.

Splitting the agent training into two 75-minute sessions is doable. We can cover the playbook overview, scripts A5, and CRM basics A3 in the first session, then focus on role plays, QA checklist A6, and escalation paths in the second. I will adjust A7 accordingly and propose a schedule that rotates through shifts over five days so we do not pull too many agents off the floor at once.

That structure sounds better. We should also include a short section on how to handle edge cases where the script does not fully apply, so agents know when they can deviate and when they must stick to the wording, especially for compliance parts. I can help draft a couple of examples for that part of A7.

I will update the account manager agenda in A7 to include a practical segment on A2 and A3, with a few role plays using real scenarios from recent deals. Scheduling the sales sessions later in the week works for me; that way we can bring in any early questions from agents and align on handovers.

For A6, I can propose a reduced set of items for the pilot: greeting, verification, needs analysis, solution clarity, one or two key compliance checks, and wrap-up. The rest can stay in the checklist as optional notes. That should make it easier for supervisors to review at least a few calls per agent each week without it becoming unmanageable.

Yes, a reduced set for the pilot is a good idea. We can define a minimum number of calls per agent per month to review using A6, maybe three to five, and then adjust once we see how much time it takes. I will add that guidance into the T11 documentation so supervisors know what is expected.

To get to D5 and D6, let me summarise the proposal. Training schedule: two 75-minute sessions for agents across shifts over five days, plus a 90-minute session for account managers later in the same week, all detailed in A7. Content includes playbook overview A1, scripts A5, CRM guide A3, qualification checklist A2, QA checklist A6, and escalation basics. QA checklist: lean version of A6 for the pilot, focusing on a core set of behaviours and compliance points, with a target of three to five calls per agent per month. Does everyone agree with this as our final training approach and QA process for the pilot

I am aligned with that summary. The split sessions and lean QA checklist should make it easier to implement without too much disruption. As long as we keep a way to flag any serious issues that come up in QA reviews, I am comfortable approving this for the pilot.

Works for me as well. The timing and content for the account manager session are fine, and the QA cadence is reasonable. I would just suggest we add a short debrief slot at the end of the first week of training to collect quick feedback from both agents and sales so we can adjust if needed.

I am on board too. The lean version of A6 should be manageable, and the training structure in A7 looks clear. The debrief idea is good; we can use it to capture any confusion around the new scripts or CRM fields before the pilot starts.

Given the feedback, I suggest we formally agree on this training schedule and format for the pilot D5 and approve the QA checklist A6 and review cadence D6. I will update A7 and A6 with the final details and share the links in the central repository so supervisors and sales leads can start planning attendance.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot rollout, including escalation paths and dashboards.

messages.text: Pilot update. We have identified one contact centre team and one sales pod to participate in the pilot for the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout project_title. We now need to confirm the pilot scope, duration, and participating teams D7, and agree on escalation criteria and SLAs for high-value leads D8. We will track pilot KPIs in the Pilot KPIs and Performance Tracking Sheet A4 and define the dashboard metrics and cadence under T6. I have drafted an initial proposal for scope and escalation in T8 and T10 for us to refine.

For pilot scope, I suggest we include all inbound calls for the top 5 contact reasons covered in A5, plus outbound follow-up calls and emails related to those interactions. That keeps it focused but still representative. For duration, one full month should give us enough volume to see trends in A4. On escalation, my initial thought is to treat leads as high-value if they meet a revenue threshold or strategic segment criteria, and set a one business day SLA for sales to pick them up.

From the contact centre side, the selected team is comfortable focusing on the top 5 contact reasons and related follow-ups. We just need to be clear in T8 about which channels are in scope for the pilot. I would propose we include phone and email, and keep chat out for now if volumes are too low to give meaningful data. For escalation, we should also define what happens if sales does not pick up a high-value lead within the SLA, so agents know how to follow up.

I agree with keeping chat out of the first pilot if volumes are low. That will make it easier to monitor quality and compliance. On escalation criteria, we should be careful not to rely only on revenue thresholds; some cases might be sensitive from a customer relationship or regulatory point of view even if the immediate value is lower. Maybe we can add a category for risk or complaint severity that also triggers escalation.

On T6, for the dashboard metrics, I propose we track at least: number of pilot interactions, conversion rate, first contact resolution, handle time, handover speed, and CRM completeness, all pulled from existing CRM fields. We can then summarise these weekly in A4 and share a simple view with the pilot teams. For escalation SLAs, I support the one business day target for high-value leads and two days for standard leads.

So far we have. Scope: top 5 contact reasons plus related follow-ups, phone and email only. Duration: one month. Participating teams: one defined contact centre team and one sales pod. For escalation criteria in T10, we can combine revenue threshold, strategic segment, and risk or complaint severity as triggers. For SLAs, one business day for high-value leads and two for standard leads, with a clear follow-up path if the SLA is missed. Does that capture the main points

Yes, that matches my understanding. For the follow-up path when SLAs are missed, I suggest that if a high-value lead is not picked up within one business day, the system or agent flags it to the sales pod lead, and if it is still not actioned within another day, the contact centre supervisor is notified so they can decide whether to reassign or call the customer back.

That escalation path works for us. We will need to make sure agents know how to tag high-value leads correctly in the CRM, based on the criteria in T10 and the fields defined in A3. We can cover that in training A7 and reinforce it in team huddles during the first week of the pilot.

I am ok with the combined criteria for high-value leads. For the risk or complaint severity trigger, we should give agents a simple rule of thumb, for example, any complaint that could lead to formal escalation or legal risk should be tagged as high-value for follow-up. We can refine the wording with compliance, but we should not overcomplicate it for the pilot.

On T6, I can help set up a simple weekly export from the CRM to feed A4, focusing on the metrics you listed. We can then create a one-page summary for the pilot teams each week, highlighting trends and any areas where we need to coach or adjust scripts.

To close D7, can we confirm. Pilot scope: phone and email interactions for the top 5 contact reasons and related follow-ups, using the new scripts and templates from A5. Duration: one calendar month from the go-live date. Participating teams: the named contact centre team and the named sales pod we have already aligned with their managers. If everyone is comfortable with that, I will record D7 as agreed.

Confirmed from the contact centre side. The team is aware and ready to start on the agreed date, assuming training is completed as per A7. We will also brief them on the escalation rules from T10 before go-live.

Confirmed from the sales side as well. The sales pod is aligned on the one-month duration and the scope. We will make sure they are familiar with A2, A3, and A5 before the pilot starts so handovers run smoothly.

For D8, summarising the escalation criteria and SLAs. A lead is treated as high-value if it meets at least one of these. 1) Above a defined revenue threshold. 2) Belongs to a strategic segment. 3) Involves a high-risk or severe complaint. SLA. high-value leads to be picked up by sales within one business day, standard leads within two business days. If a high-value lead is not picked up within the SLA, it is flagged to the sales pod lead, and if still not actioned within another day, the contact centre supervisor is notified to decide on reassignment or proactive follow-up. If there are no objections, I will record this as our agreed escalation criteria and SLAs for the pilot.

No objections from me. I will help make sure the sales pod understands these rules and that we have a simple way to see any overdue high-value leads in our regular CRM views, even if we are not changing the core platform.
I am aligned as well. We should just make sure the training materials A7 and the playbook A1 clearly describe these criteria and SLAs so agents and supervisors know what to do in practice.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate learnings from pilot and confirm go-live plan for full rollout.

messages.text: Pilot completion update. The one-month pilot for the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout project_title has finished. Preliminary results in the Pilot KPIs and Performance Tracking Sheet A4 show. 1) Conversion rate from qualified opportunity to sale up by 9 percent. 2) First contact resolution for top 5 reasons up by 6 percentage points. 3) Average handle time roughly flat. 4) Handover speed for high-value leads improved, with 88 percent picked up within the one-day SLA. 5) CRM data completeness on mandatory fields at 93 percent. 6) QA scores slightly up. We now need to confirm whether these results meet the success criteria we agreed earlier D1 and align on the go-live plan, including updating the unified playbook A1, finalising T9 and T12, and using the rollout communication plan A8.

From the contact centre perspective, the results look positive. Agents reported that the scripts in A5 made calls more structured, though a few felt the complaint scripts were still a bit long. QA scores in A6 improved slightly, mainly due to better verification and wrap-up. We did see a few cases where escalation rules in T10 were not followed perfectly, usually when calls were very busy. We can address that with targeted coaching before full rollout.

I agree the numbers are encouraging and within the success criteria we set. From a compliance angle, the QA reviews did not surface any major issues with the new scripts, which is reassuring. We had a few minor wording tweaks suggested by compliance during the pilot, but nothing that would block a broader rollout. We should incorporate those into A5 and A1 before we publish the final playbook.

On the sales side, the uplift in conversion is consistent with what we saw in individual deals. The qualification checklist A2 helped us focus on better opportunities, and the email templates from A5, especially the shorter versions, had higher reply rates. The main feedback from the sales pod is that they would like a bit more flexibility in the follow-up cadence, which we can capture as guidance in A1 rather than strict rules.

Comparing the pilot results in A4 to the success criteria we agreed earlier for D1. 1) Conversion and handover speed both improved. 2) QA scores and handle time did not deteriorate. 3) First contact resolution and CRM completeness improved. Based on that, I would say the pilot met and slightly exceeded our targets. Unless anyone disagrees, I propose we reconfirm that the pilot KPIs meet the agreed success criteria for full rollout D1 and move ahead with planning the go-live.

I support that conclusion. For the go-live plan, we should phase the rollout by team over two to three weeks, using the training approach in A7 and the communication plan A8. We can start with teams that are closest to the pilot team so they can share experiences, then expand to the rest. I can take the lead on updating the unified playbook document T9 with the final scripts, processes, and escalation rules.

Phased rollout makes sense. We should also keep the QA checklist A6 and KPI tracking in A4 running weekly for at least the first month after go-live, so we can spot any dips early. I can help review the final version of A1 to make sure all compliance-related notes and edge cases are captured clearly.

For T12, I can draft the communication plan for full rollout using A8 as the base. It will include key messages for agents and sales, timelines for each wave, and who to contact for support. I will also highlight the pilot results from A4 so people see the benefits, not just the changes. We can then review it with contact centre supervisors before sending anything out.

I can help by adding a short FAQ section to the communication plan T12, based on questions we heard during the pilot. That should reduce uncertainty and make it easier for teams to adopt the new playbook. We can also include a link to A1 and A5 so people know where to find the latest versions.

In terms of next steps, I suggest. 1) 269042 and 8337 finalise the unified playbook document T9, consolidating A2, A3, A5, A6, escalation rules, and training references. 2) 29962 and 356759 finalise the rollout communication plan T12 using A8. 3) We agree on a go-live date and rollout waves, and keep using A4 to monitor KPIs weekly for at least the first month after full rollout. Does that cover the main actions
Yes, that works. I will start consolidating T9 today and share a draft of A1 for review by early next week. We can then lock the final version before the first rollout wave starts.

I will prepare the first draft of the communication plan T12 by mid-week and include the FAQ and pilot highlights. Once we have feedback from contact centre supervisors, we can schedule the messages and briefings according to A8.
